the presence of donor‐specific antibodies (DSA) in the setting of negative flow cytometry (FCXM) does not impact acute rejection rates, estimated glomerular function (eGFR), or death‐censored kidney transplant graft survival.

pretransplant donor‐specific antibodies (DSA) in kidney transplant recipients without desensitisation therapy are associated with inferior renal function in the first few years after transplantation, but not with inferior death‐censored allograft survival.

in kidney and kidney– pancreas transplant recipients, pretransplant donor‐specific antibodies (DSAs) in the setting of negative cell‐based flow cytometry crossmatching do not confer a significant risk of acute rejection or graft failure.

in the absence of desensitization, the presence of donor‐specific antibodies (DSA) in the setting of negative crossmatch does not appear to have a major impact on graft survival.
